angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 699,874 km at 122.23 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.1816 +/- 0.0111 mas (same row, RUWE 0.92): 122.23 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.006 +/- 0.048 solar radii from Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1659.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract): 699,874 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.1 +/- 0.14 solar masses from Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1659.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5977 +/- 131 K from Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1659.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1659.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1659.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.474, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
